description: COMBINE the current global-best kernel (brief 0 HEAD 90eeb8f8, 6407us, with the 2-level tensor-core inner panel for n<=1024 but still routing n=2048/4096 to torch.geqrf) with brief 7's n=2048 extension (c2211dc): brief 7 brought n=2048 B=8 to 21394us = 3.47x faster than geqrf by routing it through the custom one-CTA-per-matrix batched panel + TF32 tensor-core trailing GEMMs (panel concurrency breaks cuSOLVER's serial-over-batch wall; TF32 stays well inside the loose ~5e-3 factor budget at n=2048). Add n=2048 to the supported custom path on top of the current best (n=4096 B=2 stays on geqrf since with only 2 matrices batched concurrency caps at 2x and the custom panel lags geqrf there).

COMBINE base: add n=2048 to parent A's _SUPPORTED_N, routed through parent A's 2-level micro-panel kernel (IB=8 block-WY) + TF32 trailing GEMMs (scoped n>=2048) + 512-thread panel CTA + cb=16. Panel kernel templated on launch-bounds LB so n<=1024 keeps __launch_bounds__(128,1) byte-identical; n=2048 uses LB=512. n=4096 stays geqrf. Geomean 5706.14us = 1.123x over parent A 6406.82, 23.0x over 131187 baseline. n=2048 shape=19216us (BETTER than parent B's standalone 21394us: parent A's 2-level panel beats parent B's single-level panel at n=2048 too, ~14% faster/panel). nsys: panel_factor_kernel<512> = 73.7% of n=2048 time (avg 105us/launch vs parent B 122us); trailing = genuine TF32 tensor-core cutlass3x. Validates: 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN (rankdef n=2048 scaled_factor 3.45<<20).

Template panel on micro-panel width IB. n=2048 sweeps: cb {12,16,20,24}->{22087,19216,20178,19913}us (16 best); IB {4,8,16}->{21865,19216,18888}us (16 best, reproduced 18888). IB=16 at cb=16 degenerates the 2-level split to single-level unblocked recurrence (far=0) => n=2048 prefers single-level in parent A's better barrier skeleton (single-barrier block_reduce_sum, dedicated normscratch, warp-0 T factor) over 2-level block-WY (micro-panel Gram/Tblk/W/Y overhead at cb=16 outweighs far-update parallelism). n<=1024 unchanged (IB=8, byte-identical <128,8>). Geomean 5696.21us = 1.125x over parent A 6406.82, 23.0x over baseline. n=2048 shape 18888us. Validates: 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN (rankdef n=2048 scaled 3.45).

Thread-block-CLUSTER panel for n=2048: cluster of G CTAs/matrix splits the m rows into G bands, cross-CTA norm+w_c reductions via distributed SMEM (cluster.map_shared_rank) + cluster.sync() (sm_100a). Targets the under-occupied B=8 shape (single-CTA kernel runs only 8 CTAs/148 SMs, ncu 1.6% SM throughput). CORRECT (validates clean, rankdef n=2048 scaled 3.44) but SLOWER at every G: G=2->23826, G=4->22339, G=8->timeout vs single-CTA 18888us. Per-reflector cross-CTA cluster.sync()+DSMEM latency dominates the row-parallelism — same wall brief 7 hit with cg::grid().sync(); the serial Householder chain makes cross-CTA sync a net loss even with the cheaper cluster primitive. Geomean 5815.29us (regression from trial 2 5696). Cluster kernel is committed+correct; next trial removes it and restores the single-CTA best.

Remove the regressing cluster panel (kernel + host wrapper + Python plumbing); restore the clean single-CTA best from trial 2. Forward state: n=2048 -> 512-thread CTA, IB=16 single-level recurrence in parent A's barrier skeleton, cb=16, TF32 trailing GEMMs; n<=1024 byte-identical to parent A (<128,8>); n=4096 on geqrf. Geomean 5699.88us = 1.124x over parent A 6406.82, 23.0x over baseline. n=2048 shape 18874us (vs parent B standalone 21394). nsys: panel_factor_kernel<512,16> = 73.3% of n=2048 time (avg 102us/launch, marginally < IB=8's 105us); trailing = genuine TF32 cutlass3x tensor-core. Validates: 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN. This is the brief's deliverable best.

Confirm n=4096 stays on geqrf. Tested n=4096 on the custom path (cb=12, IB=16 single-level, 512-thread CTA, TF32 trailing): validates clean (scaled_factor 0.417); my faster panel gives n=4096 B=2 = 55098us (beats parent B's 60984) but STILL LOSES to geqrf 52141us — at B=2 the batched-panel concurrency win is only 2x so geqrf wins. Adding n=4096 raised geomean to 5721 vs 5697 with geqrf, so n=4096 stays on geqrf (per brief). Forward DELIVERABLE best: geomean 5697.14us = 1.124x over parent A 6406.82, 23.0x over 131187 baseline. n=2048=18885 (custom), n=4096=52165 (geqrf), n<=1024 byte-identical to parent A. nsys saved at deliverable SHA (panel_factor_kernel<512,16> ~73-77% of n=2048, median 102us). Validates: 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN.

COMBINE DELIVERED: geomean 5697.14us (commit ff00299328c8432c11a5ed3e43616a2ba77f9a70) = 1.124x over parent A 6406.82, 23.0x over 131187 baseline. n=2048 dropped from ~52k (parent A's geqrf route) to 18885us on the custom batched panel + TF32 trailing; n<=1024 BYTE-IDENTICAL to parent A; n=4096 on geqrf. Validates fully (22 tests + 3 guards: diff-correctness, invariance, off-grid; n=2050 routes to geqrf).

INTEGRATION: added n=2048 to parent A's _SUPPORTED_N and routed it through parent A's panel kernel (NOT parent B's older single-level kernel). Templated the panel kernel on launch-bounds LB (<128,8> for n<=1024 keeps __launch_bounds__(128,1) byte-identical; <512,*> for n=2048) and on micro-panel width IB. TF32 trailing GEMMs scoped to n>=2048 (allow_tf32 flipped only around them), 512-thread panel CTA, cb=16. KEY: parent A's panel beats parent B's at n=2048 too (18885 vs 21394, ~14%/panel) thanks to its single-barrier block_reduce_sum + dedicated normscratch + warp-0 T factor.

SECONDARY TEST (does parent A's 2-level inner panel help at n=2048?): MEASURED NO. cb sweep {12,16,20,24}->{22087,19216,20178,19913}us (16 best); IB sweep {4,8,16}->{21865,19216,18888}us (16 best). IB=16 at cb=16 degenerates the 2-level micro-panel split to a single-level recurrence (far=0, the 2-level block-WY branches dead-code-eliminated at compile time) and WINS by ~1.8% over IB=8. The 2-level block-WY helps n<=1024 (cb=32, far-update amortizes) but at the SMEM-capped cb<=24 for n=2048 its micro-panel Gram/Tblk/W/Y overhead outweighs the far-update parallelism. So n=2048 best = single-level cb=16 in parent A's better barrier skeleton.

THREAD-BLOCK CLUSTER (brief 7's named under-occupancy lever): BUILT, CORRECT, REGRESSED. A cluster of G CTAs/matrix splits the m rows into G bands with cross-CTA norm+w_c reductions via distributed SMEM (cluster.map_shared_rank) + cluster.sync() (sm_100a). Validates clean (rankdef n=2048 scaled 3.44) but SLOWER at every G: G=2->23826, G=4->22339, G=8->timeout, vs single-CTA 18888us. The per-reflector cross-CTA cluster.sync()+DSMEM latency dominates the row-parallelism gained — the SAME wall brief 7 hit with the heavier cg::grid().sync(); the panel's serial Householder chain makes ANY cross-CTA sync a net loss. Removed it; forward state is the clean single-CTA path.

n=4096 CONFIRMED ON GEQRF: tested the custom path at n=4096 (cb=12, IB=16, 512 threads, TF32) — validates clean, and my faster panel gives 55098us (beats parent B's 60984) but STILL loses to geqrf 52141us (B=2: only 2x batch concurrency). Adding it raised geomean to 5721 vs 5697.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (the n=2048 panel is still 73-77% of its time, under-occupied at B=8 CTAs on 148 SMs, ncu 1.6% SM throughput / 70% CTA-barrier stalls — the bottleneck is using idle SMs without cross-CTA sync cost): (1) WARP-SPECIALIZED / persistent panel that overlaps a panel's factorization with the PRIOR panel's trailing GEMM (software pipelining the serial spine against the tensor-core trailing) — the trailing is ~27% and currently serializes after each panel. (2) TENSOR-CORE within-panel apply at a LARGER cb that needs the 2-level far-update, only reachable if SMEM is freed (e.g. keep only the active micro-panel's columns in SMEM, stream the rest) — would let cb=32 fit at n=2048 and re-activate the (currently-dead) 2-level block-WY MMA path. (3) TSQR-style tall-skinny QR on the m=2048 panel (parallel QR on row-blocks then combine) — genuinely parallel across idle SMs, needs converting the block-reflector form back to LAPACK (H,tau); fundamentally different from the cluster approach that just split reductions. (4) 1024-thread panel CTA (I capped at 512; would need normscratch enlarged to 32 for nwarps=32 — risk of barrier-stall worsening since more threads sync, but halves the per-thread reduction depth — untested). (5) n=512/1024 (5 of 12 shapes, ~10.3-10.5k each, the bulk of the geomean) are UNTOUCHED by this brief and still run parent A's kernel — they dominate the geomean and a faster n=512 panel would move the needle more than further n=2048 work. Recommend a leaderboard submit of ff00299 to confirm the combined TF32-trailing + custom-panel path is remote-safe (parent B's trial 10 used the same TF32-trailing approach).
